projects.name: gmail_cbs_cleanroom
projects.title: Gmail CBS Cleanroom
projects.description:
Create a new private AdaOS Application named "Gmail CBS Cleanroom" from
scratch, with technical id gmail_cbs_cleanroom. It must be CBS-compatible. Its
semantic Application requires capability:mail.messages.manage version ^1.0.0
without naming Gmail, a package, a skill, endpoints, account ids, or
credentials. For this first beta, realize that requirement with an
Application-local Gmail binding.

The user experience must include connection and setup status, inbox and label
navigation, search and unread/starred filters, message list and reading,
labels, archive, trash, read/unread, star/unstar, compose, and send. Include
responsive wide and compact layouts and deterministic loading, empty, offline,
provider-error, permission-denied, and authorization-required states. Explain
least-privilege access. OAuth secrets and tokens must never enter UI state,
manifests, fixtures, logs, errors, or telemetry. Keep shared provider reuse and
a global capability registry outside this first stage.

Build the executable Prototype now. Keep real external operations as explicit
pending Automation requirements; do not simulate successful authorization or
use live Gmail data in the Prototype.

projects.name: gmail_mail_client
projects.title: Gmail Mail Client
projects.description: Create a new private AdaOS Application named "Gmail Mail Client" from scratch. It must be CBS-compatible. Its semantic application requires capability:mail.messages.manage version ^1.0.0 without naming Gmail, a package, a skill, or credentials. For the first beta, implement an application-local Gmail binding. The UI must provide inbox search and filters, message reading, labels, archive, trash, compose and send, connection/setup status, explicit least-privilege disclosures, and deterministic empty/loading/error/permission-denied states. projects.name: inbox_triage
projects.title: Inbox Triage
projects.description:
Create a new private AdaOS Application named Inbox Triage, technical id mail_inbox_triage, from scratch.

Its semantic Application requires capability:mail.messages.manage version ^1.0.0. Keep semantic intent provider-, package-, skill-, account-, and credential-neutral. At materialization time reuse an installed compatible Capability Binding and its shared Core-owned connected Gmail credential through an explicit user attachment when available. Do not create, copy, fork, or edit any Gmail provider implementation. If no reusable connection exists, offer fresh OAuth setup.

This is not a mail client. It is a focused inbox triage tool: show unread messages older than seven days and optionally starred messages; show sender, subject, date, and snippet; allow explicit mark-read, archive, star/unstar, and trash actions. Do not implement compose, send, label administration, attachment browsing, or mailbox settings.

The Prototype must be safe and deterministic. Represent loading, empty, authorization-required, reusable-account-available, connected, offline, permission-denied, provider-error, and success states without contacting Gmail and without storing secrets or real mail. Provide responsive wide and compact layouts. Explain least privilege. Prototype data is disposable synthetic review data; Automation must replace it with the selected compatible binding after acceptance.

projects.name: mail_focus_reader
projects.title: Mail Focus Reader
projects.description:
Create a new private application named "Mail Focus Reader". The exact technical Application id is mail_focus_reader.

Build the shortest complete viable mail reading and triage application, not a Gmail clone. Desktop-first UI: a compact folders/labels list on the left and a message list on the right. Selecting a message replaces the list region with the message detail; an explicit Back action restores the list and preserves the selected folder. Only support read/unread, star/unstar, and archive. Do not add compose/send, OAuth settings, label administration, a local mailbox copy, or dashboard widgets.

The Application must consume the existing portable capability mail.messages.manage ^1.0.0. It must not implement Gmail API or OAuth, and its semantic Application must not name a package, provider, or skill. Reuse the installed CBS Binding/PackageDelivery and an explicitly attachable reusable Gmail credential owned by the capability/provider plane. Use bounded message summaries and progressive next-page pagination for first paint. Fetch full message content only after selection. Mutations require an explicit user gesture. Show connection status and a clear way to attach an existing Gmail connection.

Acceptance: labels load independently; the first message page performs no N+1 metadata fetch; empty, loading, and error states are visible; detail/back preserves the folder; the result can advance through beta, Trial, and workspace; Applications shows only required permissions. Prefer existing AdaOS components and the minimum number of owned artifacts.
